purpose: Provide inspectable correct-versus-wrong finished-state cues for the most failure-sensitive canonical profiles. These are diagnostic cues, not universal strength claims.

correct: braid weave is evenly tensioned around a straight leader
locking half-hitches are compact and do not walk
leader is not visibly crushed or kinked
wrong: weave slides before the locks engage
leader shows deep deformation, whitening, or a sharp kink
fg-knot.consequence: slip, guide impact, or leader damage under load

correct: outbound and return wraps stay ordered
tag exits through the leader loop in the required direction
finished barrel is compact without crossed braid
wrong: return wraps cross randomly over outbound wraps
tag exits the wrong side of the opening
barrel can be pushed or telescoped after seating

correct: two barrels seat against each other cleanly
braid side has enough wraps for the material
no tag movement appears under a hard pull test
wrong: one barrel remains open while the other is tight
braid wraps are too few or crossed
barrels pass through or separate instead of meeting

correct: two wrap columns are balanced
center tags exit in opposite directions
coils draw into a straight, symmetrical junction
wrong: one side has collapsed or overlapping wraps
diameter mismatch forces one coil to bury under the other
blood-knot.consequence: uneven leader turnover and concentrated stress

correct: leader wraps lie evenly around the doubled line
leader returns through the opening cleanly
finished knot stays streamlined against the double line
wrong: the doubled line is twisted through the barrel
knot leaves a pronounced snagging shoulder
bristol-knot.consequence: slip, abrasion, or poor guide passage

correct: doubled main-line wraps are tight and ordered
leader exits back in line after seating
wrap count matches material behavior
wrong: braid has too few wraps and can creep
leader is trapped at an angle
wraps reverse or cross during the final pull
yucatan-knot.consequence: leader slip or unstable high-load connection

correct: twist column is uniform under tension
reverse wraps progress without gaps
finished double-line loop has two balanced legs
wrong: one loop leg bears visibly more load than the other
bimini-twist.consequence: uneven load sharing or twist collapse

correct: loop legs emerge evenly
wrap bundle is compact
braid uses the higher practical wrap count required by the material
wrong: short wrap bundle in slick braid
one leg pulls ahead of the other
hitch opens or rolls when the loop is spread

correct: doubled strands remain parallel
overhand section is not crossed over itself
final loop seats around the eye/hardware without trapping against the hook point or split ring
wrong: loop catches around part of the lure or hook incorrectly
knot seats with one strand visibly tighter than the other

correct: wraps spiral neatly without overlap
tag returns through both required openings
coil slides fully to the eye during seating
wrong: coil stops above the eye and leaves an open gap

correct: wraps form a clean barrel
barrel slides to the eye without crossing
braid receives enough wraps and passes a hard slip test
wrong: coil stops partially open before reaching the hardware

correct: two eye passes stay parallel
Uni-family wraps are orderly
barrel seats against the doubled eye contact without crossing
wrong: eye passes cross inside or outside the eye
barrel is tied on only one effective eye pass
fish-n-fool-knot.consequence: abrasion at the eye or reduced slip resistance

correct: fused line remains doubled through the Palomar-style structure
double-overhand section is clean
hardware passes through the loop without twisting the doubled strands
wrong: slick strands cross or separate during seating
tag movement appears under a firm pull test

correct: wraps lie side by side on the shank
line exits the hook eye in the intended orientation
coil does not climb toward the eye under load
wrong: leader exits the wrong side of the eye for the intended hook orientation
short tag begins pulling into the wraps

correct: Uni barrel lies cleanly on the hook shank
line exits through the eye in the intended direction
wraps remain compact during a load test
wrong: line exits the eye in a direction that twists the hook
braid or slick line creeps through too few wraps

correct: true haywire twists precede barrel wraps
wire strands rotate around each other rather than one strand merely wrapping the other
tag is fatigue-broken cleanly rather than cut into a sharp burr
wrong: wire is kinked sharply at the eye
cut tag leaves a dangerous sharp burr
haywire-twist.consequence: wire fatigue, connection failure, or handling injury

correct: leader sits centered in a compatible fly-line core
core/coating is not split
external securing turns are compact and smooth
wrong: leader is forced into incompatible construction
coating splits around the insertion point
leader exits off-center or can be pulled from the core before final seating

correct: loop remains the intended size after seating
wraps form cleanly in the reviewed mono-first system
tag and standing line leave the knot without crossed coils
wrong: fluorocarbon is substituted despite the documented warning
loop size changes under a pull test

correct: mono and fluorocarbon loops twist together evenly
both line ends/leader pass through the shared opening as required
figure-eight-like finished junction is compact
wrong: braid is substituted for the mono-main system
one material cuts across the other at a sharp angle

correct: two finished loops interlock squarely
load is shared across the intended loop legs
connection can be separated without visible twist damage
wrong: one loop collapses into an accidental girth-hitch orientation
worn or damaged loop is reused
loop-to-loop-connection.consequence: localized wear, distortion, or premature loop failure

correct: loop holds the intended size after seating
wraps form cleanly around the standing line
tag returns through the overhand from the same side it exited
wrong: loop shrinks or collapses under a pull test
wraps reverse or bunch during the final draw
tag exits the overhand on the wrong path
non-slip-loop-kreh-loop.consequence: unstable loop size or sudden terminal failure

correct: fixed loop size is preserved after seating
wraps around the standing line stay ordered
final tuck locks without collapsing the loop
wrong: final tuck is omitted or reversed
rapala-knot.consequence: lost lure action or knot collapse

correct: main-line wraps stay ordered around the doubled leader
tag exits cleanly after the wrap series
finished junction is compact without telescoping
wrong: leader loop is twisted through the barrel
junction can be pushed open after seating
albright-special.consequence: slip under load or bulky guide hang

correct: two overhand passes seat squarely
both tags exit cleanly
finished knot is compact without crossed strands
wrong: knot remains open or asymmetric after pull
surgeons-knot.consequence: uneven junction or reduced holding power

correct: barrel wraps lie tightly on the fly line or leader tube
leader exits in line without a shoulder
coils do not telescope when loaded
wrong: leader exits at an angle creating a snag shoulder
barrel slides when the leader is pulled

correct: Neat spiral wraps seated to the eye
Tag exits cleanly without reverse wraps
Coil remains closed after pull test
clinch-knot.consequence: An open clinch fails on the first solid hookset.

correct: Double pass through the eye is visible
Ordered coil seats fully
Both eye passes remain parallel
trilene-knot.consequence: Missing the double pass removes the Trilene advantage.

correct: Compact half-hitch structure at the eye
Tag exits in the intended direction
Knot stays small after seating
wrong: Open hitch that walks on the eye
davy-knot.consequence: A walking Davy slips free under tippet-class loads.

correct: Second pass completes before the final draw
Compact seat at the eye
Tag controlled and short
double-davy-knot.consequence: Incomplete double structure reverts to a weaker single Davy.

correct: Figure-eight style seat looks compact
Tag and standing line exit cleanly
No open loops after pull test
wrong: Open figure-eight that did not draw down
orvis-knot.consequence: An undrawn Orvis can open on the first fish.

correct: Ordered wraps with the distinctive Pitzen draw path
Coil seats tightly to the eye
Tag exits controlled
wrong: Lost wrap order during the draw
Tag trapped in the wrong path
pitzen-knot.consequence: A misdrawn Pitzen loses the strength that justifies the knot.

correct: Long ordered wrap column for the material
Clean seat after the final tuck
No reverse wraps
san-diego-jam-knot.consequence: Short wrap count on braid is a common San Diego Jam failure.

correct: Doubled braid structure remains ordered
Wraps seat without springing open
Tag controlled after draw
berkley-braid-knot.consequence: Braid needs the doubled structure to hold under shock loads.

correct: Loop size holds after seating
Final tuck sits in the classic perfection geometry
Standing line exits in-line with the loop
wrong: Final tuck in the wrong gap
perfection-loop.consequence: A collapsed perfection loop becomes a weak overhand.

correct: Double overhand completed on the doubled line
Loop size stable after draw
Tags exit cleanly
surgeons-end-loop.consequence: Incomplete double overhand fails as a fixed loop.

correct: Loop stands perpendicular after seating
Wraps ordered around the standing line
Loop size matches intended dropper length
wrong: Too few twists before the pull-through
Standing line nicked by the pull
dropper-loop.consequence: A collapsed dropper loop fouls flies and weakens the leader.

correct: Fixed loop preserved for lure action
Wraps ordered on the standing line
Loop does not close under load
homer-rhode-loop-knot.consequence: A closed Homer Rhode removes free lure swing.

correct: Overhand on standing line seats against the spool arbor
Tag overhand stops slip under spool tension
Line cinches to the arbor without spinning free
wrong: Knot not drawn to the arbor
Wrong direction relative to spool spin
arbor-knot.consequence: A bad arbor knot slips and dumps the spool under the first run.

correct: Enhanced arbor structure fully seated
No slip under spool tension test
Tags controlled
wrong: Spins on the arbor under tension
100-percent-arbor-knot.consequence: Incomplete arbor structure can free-spool under hard runs.

correct: Both doubled sides form compact barrels
Barrels meet squarely
Tags exit cleanly
double-double-uni-knot.consequence: Missing the double on one side creates an asymmetric weak join.

correct: Bimini or double-line side present as intended
Ordered wraps with slim profile
Tags trimmed clean
slim-beauty-knot.consequence: Without the double-line foundation the slim profile fails under load.

correct: Ordered multi-wrap join with clean exits
Junction stays slim after seating
No reverse wraps
j-knot.consequence: A crossed J Knot becomes a cutting join under diameter step.

correct: Quick wrap structure fully completed
Seated without open loops
Tags controlled
aussie-quickie.consequence: An incomplete quick join can dump a fish on the first run.

correct: Side-by-side shank wraps
Intended eye exit orientation
Hook alignment stable after pull
easy-snell-knot.consequence: A bad snell points the hook off-line and weakens the set.

correct: Hair or bait attachment path correct
Shank wraps ordered
Exit direction matches intended presentation
knotless-knot.consequence: Misbuilt knotless geometry ruins hair presentation and strength.

correct: Loop sized for bait holds after seating
Shank wraps ordered
Loop does not collapse
egg-loop-knot.consequence: A collapsed egg loop dumps bait on the first cast.

correct: Fixed loop geometry preserved
Wraps ordered
Loop action free at the lure
king-sling.consequence: Closed loop removes the free-swing action the knot is for.

correct: Plaited double-line section uniform
Locking finish secure
Legs share load
australian-plait.consequence: A gappy plait concentrates load on one leg and fails early.

correct: Tippet join seats compactly
Tags exit cleanly
No cutting angle at the junction
orvis-tippet-knot.consequence: A poorly seated tippet join is a classic dry-fly failure point.

correct: Ordered wraps with intended return path
Compact slim junction
Tags controlled
willis-knot.consequence: Crossed Willis wraps become a cutting join under load.

correct: Terminal structure fully completed for the eye
Seated coil without gaps
Tag controlled
baja-knot.consequence: An incomplete Baja terminal can dump a lure on the cast.

correct: Distinctive Centauri geometry seated
Clean tag exit
No open loops
centauri-knot.consequence: A misdrawn Centauri loses the geometry that gives it strength.

correct: Loop seats behind a down-eye or turned-up eye as intended
Knot draws up cleanly on the eye neck
Fly rides true
wrong: Used on a straight-eye where it does not seat
turle-knot.consequence: Wrong eye type or incomplete seat ruins fly tracking.

correct: Completed figure geometry seated at the eye
Tag controlled
No open segments
world-fair-knot.consequence: Incomplete World Fair geometry fails early under tippet loads.

correct: Full sequence completed
Compact seat
Tag controlled
jacks-knot.consequence: An incomplete Jack's Knot is unreliable on the first fish.

correct: Eye-crossing path completed as designed
Seated without open loops
Tag exit correct
eye-crosser-knot.consequence: Missing the eye-cross path removes the knot's holding geometry.

correct: Dry-fly terminal geometry seated small and clean
Fly rides true
Tag short and controlled
harvey-dry-fly-knot.consequence: A bulky Harvey terminal kills dry-fly drift and can fail on take.

correct: Multiple eye passes ordered
Compact final structure
Parallel strands where intended
jansik-special.consequence: Lost pass count on a Jansik Special is a sudden failure mode.

correct: Hitch orientation matches intended wake direction
Holds position behind the eye
Does not flip under light tension
wrong: Hitch on the wrong side of the eye
riffle-hitch.consequence: Wrong hitch side wakes the fly the wrong way—or not at all.

correct: Stopper grips the line without cutting
Position holds after cast pressure
Coils neat and short
bobber-stopper-knot.consequence: A sliding stopper ruins depth control; an over-tight one nicks main line.

correct: Double-line foundation present
Ordered wraps on the swivel eye
Seated without open loops
offshore-swivel-knot.consequence: Single-line offshore connections are a classic big-fish failure.

correct: Two compact barrels for indicator join
Barrels meet cleanly
Tags controlled
strike-indicator-double-uni.consequence: An open indicator join dumps the indicator mid-drift.

correct: Loop holds indicator as intended
Size stable after seating
No collapse under cast
strike-indicator-loop-knot.consequence: A collapsed indicator loop loses the fly's depth reference.

correct: Level line and tippet join seats cleanly
No cutting angle
Connection slim enough for the rod
tenkara-level-line-connection.consequence: A bulky tenkara join kills presentation and can fail on soft tippet.

correct: Traditional join geometry completed
Seated without open segments
Tags controlled
tenkara-traditional-line-connection.consequence: Incomplete traditional tenkara joins fail on the first solid take.

correct: Tool-formed barrel tight on host
In-line leader exit
No telescope after load
knot-tyer-nail-knot.consequence: A loose tool nail knot slides or cuts the host under load.

render_rule: Show correct cues and wrong cues together. Where visual_priority is p0, produce a dedicated original correct-vs-wrong SVG before public release; p1 may launch with textual inspection cues if the base instructional SVG is already clear.
